import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# --- Data Preparation for Visualization ---
# Map numerical columns to more descriptive strings for clearer labels
df['Survival Status'] = df['survived'].map({0: 'Did not survive', 1: 'Survived'})
df['Passenger Class'] = df['pclass'].map({1: 'First', 2: 'Second', 3: 'Third'})

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the overall aesthetic style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", font_scale=1.1)

# Create a FacetGrid to show multiple relationships in one figure
g = sns.FacetGrid(df, col="Passenger Class", hue="Survival Status",
                  col_order=['First', 'Second', 'Third'],
                  hue_order=['Survived', 'Did not survive'],
                  palette={'Survived': '#588B8B', 'Did not survive': '#C8553D'},
                  height=6, aspect=0.7)

# Map a scatter plot to the grid, showing the relationship between age and fare
g.map(sns.scatterplot, 'age', 'fare', alpha=0.7, s=60, edgecolor='w', linewidth=0.5)

# --- Customization and Annotations ---
# Set the overall title for the plot
g.fig.suptitle('Titanic Survival Analysis: Age, Fare, and Class', fontsize=20, y=1.03, weight='bold')

# Customize axis labels and titles
g.set_axis_labels("Age of Passenger", "Fare (in British Pounds)")
g.set_titles(col_template="{col_name} Class", size=14)

# Format the y-axis (Fare) to be more readable
for ax in g.axes.flat:
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(mticker.FuncFormatter(lambda x, p: f'£{int(x)}'))
    ax.grid(linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)

# Add a clear legend
g.add_legend(title='Survival Status', label_order=['Survived', 'Did not survive'], fontsize=12)
g.legend.get_title().set_fontsize(13)

# Add an insightful annotation to the First Class plot
ax1 = g.axes[0, 0]
ax1.annotate('Higher fares in First Class\ncorrelate with higher survival rates,\nespecially for older passengers.',
             xy=(40, 250), xytext=(10, 400),
             arrowprops=dict(facecolor='black', arrowstyle="->", connectionstyle="arc3,rad=.2"),
             fontsize=11, bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.3", fc="ivory", ec="gray", lw=1, alpha=0.8))

# Save the final figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
